name: Hydrocarbon (non-halogenated) solvents
label: HC
description: Organic solvents with no halogens, e.g. hexane, petroleum ether, toluene, xylene, ethanol, methanol, isopropanol, acetone, acetonitrile, ethyl acetate, DMSO.
instructions: Pour in the fume hood using a funnel. Never mix with oxidisers or halogenated waste. Cap the container afterwards.

name: Chlorinated solvents
label: Cl
description: Solvents containing chlorine, e.g. dichloromethane (DCM), chloroform, carbon tetrachloride, chlorobenzene.
instructions: Pour in the fume hood using a funnel. Keep separate from hydrocarbon waste and log the volume.

name: Halogenated solvents
label: X
description: Solvents containing bromine, fluorine or iodine (and chlorine if the lab has no separate chlorinated container), e.g. bromoform, iodomethane, fluorinated solvents.
instructions: Pour in the fume hood using a funnel. Keep separate from hydrocarbon waste and log the volume.

name: Aqueous waste
label: AQ
description: Water-based solutions containing acids, bases, salts or dissolved non-heavy-metal chemicals.
instructions: Check the pH and neutralise if your lab requires it. Never pour down the sink unless explicitly permitted.

name: Acid waste
label: ACID
description: Strong or concentrated acids: HCl, H2SO4, HNO3, neat TFA or formic acid.
instructions: Keep apart from bases, bleach, azide, cyanides and organics. Do not neutralise unless your SOP permits.

name: Alkaline waste
label: BASE
description: Strong bases such as NaOH or KOH solutions, roughly pH 11 and above.
instructions: Keep apart from acids and aluminium. Do not neutralise unless your SOP permits.

name: Sink (drain with flush)
label: SINK
bin: Sink, flushed with plenty of water
description: Small volumes of non-hazardous aqueous waste: neutral buffers (TBST, TAE without stain, running buffer), diluted used bleach.
instructions: Flush with plenty of water. Only if your lab permits drain disposal.

name: Silver nitrate waste
label: AgNO₃
description: Silver nitrate solutions and silver residues, e.g. from halide tests or Tollens' reagent (Tollens' must be destroyed with dilute acid first, never stored).
instructions: Collect separately so the silver can be recovered. Wear gloves: it stains skin. Never store ammoniacal silver solutions.

name: Heavy metal waste
label: Pb/Hg
description: Solutions or solids containing heavy metals such as lead, mercury, cadmium, chromium, copper, nickel or cobalt.
instructions: Collect separately and label with the metals present. Mercury spills: stop and call a technician.

name: Silica waste
label: SiO₂
description: Used silica gel from columns, TLC plates and silica-contaminated cotton wool or sand.
instructions: Let solvent evaporate in the fume hood first. Bag dry silica and avoid creating dust; wear a mask if needed.

name: Guanidinium / phenol lysis waste
label: GUA
bin: Dedicated labelled carboy (never shared with bleach waste)
description: TRIzol aqueous phase, kit lysis and binding buffers containing guanidinium.
instructions: Never add bleach: toxic gas. Keep in its own labelled carboy.

name: CMR liquids
label: CMR
bin: Sealed labelled bottle in secondary containment
description: Carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic liquids: acrylamide solution, EtBr buffers, formaldehyde/PFA, DAB, trypan blue.
instructions: Seal, label every constituent, keep in secondary containment. Never down the drain.

name: CMR solids
label: CMR
description: Solids contaminated with CMR agents: EtBr gels, EtBr/DAB gloves and tips, trypan blue slides.
instructions: Double bag, seal and label. Never autoclave.

name: Reactive / unstable chemicals
label: REACT
description: Water-reactive, peroxide-forming, explosive or azide solids: acetic anhydride, old ether/THF, picric acid, sodium azide.
instructions: Never mix with anything. Old peroxide formers and dry picric acid must not be moved: report them to the lab safety officer.

name: Cytotoxic waste
label: CYTO
bin: Purple-lidded bin / purple bag (and purple-lidded sharps)
description: Waste and sharps exposed to cytotoxic or cytostatic drugs.
instructions: Keep in its own purple stream. Never autoclave or drain.

name: Autoclave (biological) waste
label: BIO
description: Microbial cultures, petri dishes, agar plates, plastic loops, tips and gloves contaminated with biological material.
instructions: Place in the autoclave bag. Liquid cultures must be disinfected or autoclaved first. Never add chemicals or sharps.

name: Biological liquids
label: BIO-L
description: Aspirated media, supernatants and PBS/trypsin washes with biological material and no hazardous additives.
instructions: Inactivate with disinfectant per your SOP, then drain; never autoclave once bleach is added.

name: GM waste
label: GM
description: Transfected or virally transduced cells and GM-contaminated consumables and liquids.
instructions: Inactivate before it leaves the lab and label as GM, per your GM risk assessment.

name: Clinical waste (incineration)
label: CLIN
description: Human or animal tissue, FFPE blocks, unfixed samples.
instructions: Seal, label and hold for clinical waste collection.

name: Sharps
label: SHARPS
description: Needles, syringes with needles, scalpel and razor blades, glass Pasteur pipettes, microscope slides and cover slips.
instructions: Do not recap needles. Drop straight into the sharps bin and never fill past the line.

name: Clean glass
label: GLASS
description: Uncontaminated glass: rinsed empty bottles, clean broken glassware, clean slides, coverslips and Pasteur pipettes.
instructions: Empty bottles: triple-rinse (rinse goes to the right liquid waste), remove the cap and deface the label. Broken glass: use a dustpan or tongs, never bare hands. Contaminated glass goes in sharps instead.

name: Chemically contaminated solids
label: SOLID
description: Gloves, paper towels, weighing boats and filter paper with chemical residue.
instructions: Bag and seal. Do not put in general waste.

name: Recycling
description: Clean cardboard packaging, paper and uncontaminated plastic bottles.
instructions: Flatten boxes. Only recycle containers that held non-hazardous contents.

name: General waste
label: GEN
description: Clean, uncontaminated non-recyclable items such as food wrappers and clean tissues.
instructions: Only if it has never touched chemicals or biological material.

name: Pharmaceutical waste
label: PHARM
description: Expired or unused non-cytotoxic medicines.
instructions: Keep in original packaging where possible.

name: Surplus reagents (lab pack)
label: PACK
bin: Original container, listed on the lab-pack inventory
description: Surplus or unwanted reagents still in their original containers.
instructions: Keep the original label and add it to the lab-pack inventory.

name: Reuse / redistribute
label: REUSE
description: Unopened, in-date surplus reagents and consumables.
instructions: Offer on the chemical exchange shelf before disposing.

name: Supplier take-back
label: BACK
description: Polystyrene boxes, clean cool packs and supplier packaging.
instructions: Return through the supplier take-back scheme.

name: Electrical equipment (WEEE)
label: WEEE
description: Old electronic equipment such as plate readers and power supplies.
instructions: Decontaminate and tag before collection.

name: Batteries
label: BATT
description: Instrument and pipette-controller batteries.
instructions: Tape the terminals of lithium batteries.

name: Lamps and UV tubes
label: LAMP
description: UV bulbs, fluorescent tubes, transilluminator lamps.
instructions: Keep intact; they contain mercury.

name: Gas cylinders
label: GAS
description: Empty or unwanted gas cylinders.
instructions: Never put in any bin. Return to the supplier or cylinder store.
